claims.text: Dietary phosphate restriction to 0.8-1 g/day usually normalizes phosphate when eGFR < 60;
claims.quote: Phosphate restriction to 0.8 to 1 g/day of dietary intake is typically sufficient to normalize serum phosphate level in patients with eGFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m 2

claims.text: Calcium-containing (eg, calcium acetate) or non-calcium (eg, sevelamer) binders.
claims.quote: calcium-containing [eg, calcium acetate] or non–calcium-containing [eg, sevelamer]

claims.text: Non-calcium binders are preferred with hypercalcemia, suspected adynamic bone disease or vascular calcification.
claims.quote: Non–calcium-containing binders are preferred in patients with hypercalcemia, suspected adynamic bone disease, or evidence of vascular calcification on imaging

claims.text: With calcium-containing binders, total dietary + medication calcium should stay <= 2000 mg/day at eGFR < 60.
claims.quote: If calcium-containing binders are prescribed, then the total dietary and medication sources of calcium should not exceed 2000 mg/day in patients with eGFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m 2
